weather_line: Crisp in the hollows · a scarf-wearing wind from the northeast

stories.headline: Second Duck Found Accessorised; Scarf Matches Nothing in the Known Wizarding World; the Jeep Community Is Alarmed
body: A second duck has been dressed. Witnesses arriving at the vehicle early Friday morning discovered that the small ceramic duck known informally as 'the Admiral' — positioned third from the left on the Jeep's rear shelf since mid-August — was now wearing a miniature captain's hat of unknown provenance. The hat fits perfectly. This detail has unsettled everyone.

The orange knitted scarf on the twelfth duck remains in place and shows no sign of Summoning Charm interference. A textile analysis conducted by the Magical Fibres desk has confirmed what was already suspected: the wool matches no known manufacturer in Diagon Alley, Hogsmeade, or the three catalogues Christine keeps filed by year. 'It's not a bad scarf,' one analyst admitted, before being asked not to editorialize.

The broader wizarding Jeep community has now weighed in. Two separate owners — one in Ottery St Catchpole, one filing from an unspecified location near a ridge — have reported similar incidents: ducks appearing overnight in new positions, one with a ribbon, one simply moved six inches to the right for reasons that remain philosophically troubling. The Duck Bandit is not local. The Duck Bandit has range.

stories.section: Home & Infrastructure · The Porch Railing Situation
stories.headline: Adam Arrives Tomorrow; the Railing Has Spent Friday in Contemplative Silence; Don's Portrait Is Ready
body: With Adam's arrival confirmed for Saturday morning, the household entered Friday in a state of calibrated anticipation. Steve has positioned the level on the workbench where it will be easily located. He has not touched the northeast corner post. He is, sources confirm, 'giving it the night.'

Don's portrait spent much of Friday afternoon facing the diagram it produced Wednesday, making small sounds of satisfaction. When asked whether he had any concerns about tomorrow's inspection, the portrait replied that he had no concerns, that the oak was good oak, and that whoever specified the bracket clearly hadn't held a real piece of wood recently. The portrait was then asked to stop specifying, and it did, but not immediately.

The railing issued no statement. Christine's household ledger entry for Friday reads: 'Railing: quiet. Adam: Saturday. Level: located. Don: confident. Steve: ready.' The ledger is, as always, complete.

stories.headline: Friday Client Arrives with a Binder; Christine Notes the Binder Approvingly; the Goblins Have Already Photocopied It
body: In what the Senior Client Liaison's office is informally calling 'a very good Friday,' Christine's ten o'clock appointment arrived carrying a colour-coded binder containing tabbed documentation of every transaction in question, a summary letter, and — in a touch that was described by one junior goblin as 'almost moving' — a spare quill.

Christine received the binder. She opened it. She turned to Tab C without being directed. The client, who had clearly spent Wednesday evening preparing, watched this happen with the expression of someone who has finally, finally been understood.

By the time the goblin clerks had finished making copies — a process initiated without being asked, which has not happened in recorded Gringotts history — the matter was resolved and both parties had left. The binder remains in the office. It is being studied.

stories.headline: Gorge Notes Arrival of Proper Autumn; the Fog Has Put On Its Good Configuration; Eleven Ducks Reported Wearing No Accessories Whatsoever, a Fact Now Under Review
body: The Red River Gorge filed its Friday bulletin at dawn, confirming that autumn has now taken full occupancy of the ridgelines and will not be accepting appeals. The fog, described by the Gorge's filing officer as 'settled and purposeful,' has adopted the long low configuration associated with October expeditions and is believed to be approximately two weeks ahead of schedule. The Gorge is not apologising for this.

In light of the Duck Bandit developments, the Gorge bulletin included an unusual appendix: a report that all eleven ducks stationed at the Jellico trailhead camp were inspected Friday morning and found to be 'unadorned.' The filing officer noted this seemed relevant. It is relevant. The Duck Bandit has not been to Jellico — or has been to Jellico and chosen, for reasons of their own, to leave it alone. Both interpretations are troubling.

familiars_corner: Lucy: The textile analyst's report on the duck scarves has been left on the kitchen table. Lucy has read it. Lucy has opinions about the wool that she is keeping entirely to herself.

Ellie: Ellie discovered the Admiral duck's new hat this morning, approached it with great curiosity, and then sat down in front of the Jeep for eleven minutes waiting for the hat to do something. It did not do something. Ellie remains open to the possibility that it will.

Jersey: The workbench has been cleared to accommodate the level for tomorrow's inspection. Jersey has assessed the cleared space and relocated there immediately. The level is underneath him. He considers this resolved.
founding_editor_note: The oak was kiln-dried. I checked it. The level will confirm what I already know, and that will be that. — D.

in_brief.sport: The Holyhead Harpies have postponed Saturday's match due to what the league is calling 'unprecedented accessory interference on the pitch.' No further details have been provided. The ducks are not considered suspects at this time.
in_brief.forecast: Friday evening: crisp, clear, faintly conspiratorial. Saturday: inspection weather. One scarf-shaped cloud visible from the northeast at dusk, moving with intent.

storyline_updates.title: The Porch Railing Situation
storyline_updates.summary: Day 4 (Friday): The railing spent the day in silence. Steve has located the level. Don's portrait is confident. Adam arrives Saturday. Resolution files Saturday: the joint inspection, the level, the oak, the bracket question, a verdict that is satisfying, funny, and slightly vindicating for Don. Resolve this arc in Saturday's edition.

storyline_updates.title: The Duck Bandit Chronicles
storyline_updates.summary: Day 2: A second duck (the Admiral) has been given a miniature captain's hat of unknown origin. The orange-scarf twelfth duck remains dressed. The wool matches no known manufacturer. Two other wizarding Jeep owners in separate locations have reported similar incidents — a ribbon, a moved duck — suggesting the Duck Bandit operates regionally, possibly nationally. The Gorge ducks were found unadorned Friday morning. Day 3 should develop the Bandit's apparent methodology or motivation — perhaps a pattern emerges across the accessorised ducks (they all share something in common), or a witness account surfaces, or the hat's provenance is partially traced.
